Most transmission towers like that are some form of guyed mast. Basically, it's strong enough to support its own weight vertically, but being so thin, has nowhere near enough shear strength to resist lateral loads (i.e. wind). Solution, high-tension steel cables at equal angles around the structure. At that height, it will have one set near the top, and probably at least another set (if not two) spaced further down to keep it from buckling.
